To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

supersonic two-phase flows of liquid-gas mixtures with volume ratios around 10:1 are characterized by the following : (1) The local sound velocity is reduced by a factor of 1.5 over that of the gaseous component, and the flow model changes from the gaseous to the dispersed liquid-gas model as the volume ratio decreases from 1:1 to 10:1, with a corresponding increase in sound velocity.
supersonic two-phase flows of gas and dispersed liquid having volume ratios near 10:1 are isothermal continuum flows, and that the flow model matrix changes at ratios near 1.1.
the continuum model is applicable to two-phase flow at supersonic velocities for volume ratios near unity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the fundamental characteristics of supersonic flow of two-phase liquid and gas mixtures in a continuum flow model.
the development of an experimental and theoretical understanding of the supersonic flow of a liquid-gas mixture.
the development of a two-phase supersonic tunnel for the study of shock phenomena in homogeneous two-phase flows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supersonic two-phase flows of liquid and gas mixtures are continuum flows in the sense that the isothermal continuum model of the flow is applicable to such flows.

a supersonic two-phase flow of liquid and gas is a continuum flow with greatly reduced sound propagative velocity, and that the continuum theory of supersonic flow is applicable to such a flow provided the volume ratio does not deviate too greatly from unity.
the supersonic flow phenomena in the two-phase flow model are well defined, and that the continuum theory of supersonic flow can be extended to such flows for volume ratios approaching 50-50.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the continuum flow model is applicable to supersonic two-phase flows of volume ratios near unity.
the isothermal continuum model is valid for volume ratios near the 1: 1 value.
a continuum theory for two-phase flow is applicable over a large portion of the flow spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the continuum theory is applicable to supersonic two-phase flows of liquid and gas having volume ratios near 0.5, and that the flow model matrix changes at volume ratios near 50 percent.
the flow of a mixture of dispersed liquid and gaseous bubbles at volume ratios near 50:50 can be treated in the continuum sense with a greatly reduced value of sound velocity.
the continuum theory is applicable to supersonic flows of two-phase mixtures of liquid and gas, and that such flows are not subject to the limitations of the classical continuum theory.
